subject: SIG network proofpack and private-endpoint affirmation
messages:
From: Daniel Ortiz <daniel.ortiz@praxisfin.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 1 Aug 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: SIG follow-up — network details we still need

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for getting the SIG questionnaire over last week. Our procurement/security team did a quick pass and they requested a small set of artefacts for the network section before we close SOC/SIG intake:

- Confirmation of whether you support VPC peering vs PrivateLink in prod (we need the preferred path).
- The public IP ranges (or NAT IPs) your outbound connections will egress from for our allowlist.
- A short annotated topology diagram showing private endpoints and any transitive routing (if present).
- Any config snippets or Terraform references for your PrivateLink connector.

Can you share these items or a single package that covers them? We need to attach it to the SIG packet by EOW (Fri 6 Aug).

Thanks,
Daniel
Daniel Ortiz
Senior Security Engineer — Praxis Financial
security@praxisfin.com

--
Attachment: "praxis-sig-ask.pdf" (1 page request summary)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Ortiz <daniel.ortiz@praxisfin.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Aug 2027 10:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up — network details we still need

Hi Daniel — thanks for the clear ask. I started a small "network proofpack" that should cover everything; attaching a first cut.

Quick summary in case you want a TL;DR:
- Preferred production connectivity: PrivateLink (AWS NLB-backed Private Endpoints) by default; we offer VPC peering on a case-by-case basis for large dedicated deployments.
- Outbound egress NAT IPs: we can provide a short CSV of NAT/egress IPs.
- Topology: included annotated diagram (privatelink endpoints placed in a dedicated infra VPC; traffic to Redwood control plane is over TLS and can be routed over private connectivity where customers choose Dedicated or Private deployment).
- Connector/config: included a sample connector properties file and a short Terraform example for reference.

Attachments in this draft: redwood-sig-network-proofpack-draft.pdf, vpc-topology-annotated.png, privatelink-connector-example.txt

Karthik / Marcus — can you review the NAT IP list I assembled (sheet tab "egress-ips-draft") and confirm these are the stable ranges we should publish for Praxis? I flagged two ranges as "ephemeral" — see notes in the proofpack.

Daniel — if this draft looks close to what you need I can finalize the CSV and a one-page cover note for your packet.

Thanks,
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Enterprise Security & Trust — Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192

--
Attachments: "redwood-sig-network-proofpack-draft.pdf" (24 pages, annotated answers), "vpc-topology-annotated.png" (diagram), "privatelink-connector-example.txt" (config snippet)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Daniel Ortiz <daniel.ortiz@praxisfin.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Aug 2027 08:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up — network details we still need

Soojin / Daniel — I reviewed the egress list and made a couple of corrective notes.

Confirmed stable egress ranges for Hosted API (us-west-2 edge and NLB egress):
- 34.208.128.0/18
- 52.23.0.0/16
- 18.204.0.0/16

Marked ephemeral ranges (do not publish for allowlist unless you want transient windows):
- 3.8.200.0/22 (ephemeral burst pool)

Also: for PrivateLink connectors we publish the interface endpoint DNS names and the connector requires customers to allow TCP 443 only to our NLB; no other ports are required. The privatelink-connector-example.txt contains the minimal properties used during provisioning.

I attached a trimmed CSV with the stable ranges and a short note for the SIG packet.

Karthik
Principal SRE — Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: "ip-allowlist-2027-08-04.csv" (stable ranges)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Ortiz <daniel.ortiz@praxisfin.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2027 16:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Final: SIG network proofpack and allowlist (PRX-459)

Hi Daniel — attaching the finalized proofpack for your SIG packet. This incorporates Karthik's corrections and a short cover note that explains the PrivateLink-first posture and the case where we offer VPC peering (Dedicated / large private deployments only).

Included:
- redwood-sig-network-proofpack.pdf — final answers and annotated security notes (24 pages)
- vpc-topology-annotated.png — final diagram with endpoint placement
- ip-allowlist-2027-08-09.csv — stable egress IP ranges for allowlisting
- privatelink-connector-config.txt — minimal connector config and Terraform snippet

A few helpful points for your packet:
- If Praxis requires strict IP allowlist only for control-plane callbacks, use the CSV above. If you need total egress coverage for outbound model-serving requests (edge CDN -> customer backend) flag that in procurement and we can generate a per-account egress view (requires Dedicated or Private deployments).
- We have a short SLA exception routing if PrivateLink cannot be used; Marcus is the contact for architecture exceptions.

Please confirm receipt and whether this is sufficient for the SIG intake. Happy to hop on a 15-min call if your team wants a quick walkthrough.

Best,
Soojin

--
Attachments: "redwood-sig-network-proofpack.pdf","vpc-topology-annotated.png","ip-allowlist-2027-08-09.csv","privatelink-connector-config.txt"
